news.title: Pune: 11 PGs, hostels sealed in Lohegaon over fire safety violations
news.para: The inspections were launched against the backdrop of recent fatal fires at PG accommodations and private coaching centres in major cities like Delhi, Mumbai, and Amravati. Officials said the safety drive will soon be extended to other parts of the city.

news.title: Ranchi civic body to install 5,300 LED street lights across city
news.para: The civic body has floated a tender inviting eligible companies to supply, install, test and commission LED street lights of 75 W, 90 W and 120 W capacities. The contract also includes related services and three years of comprehensive maintenance.

news.title: Prayagraj civic body approves land bank, fee hikes, reforms
news.para: Prayagraj Municipal Corporation will prepare its own land bank for future city projects.  A 150% fee will be charged for illegal possession of municipal shops.  Unipoles and LED displays will be installed at key transport hubs for revenue.  A one-time fee of Rs 1,000 is approved for delayed property mutation.  A committee will examine faulty electrical equipment purchased since 2023.

news.title: Chandigarh's amended master plan gives industrial areas more space, more uses
news.para: Chandigarh's industrial areas are on the brink of a remarkable overhaul thanks to upcoming development strategies. Amended Master Plans will permit enhanced construction within current industrial zones. Mixed-use developments may emerge in Phase III areas, fostering new economic activities. Alongside, a revamped industrial policy will present financial incentives and utility benefits to attract businesses. These initiatives are designed to amplify investment and refresh the city's industrial environment.

news.title: Tamil Nadu RERA not civil court to decide title dispute: Madras HC
news.para: The Madras High Court clarified that TNRERA registrations do not interfere with civil title disputes, which must be handled by qualified civil courts. The court denied a request to overturn the TNRERA registration for a Tambaram property, citing the project's progress in construction. Consequently, the challenge against the registration has been resolved, upholding the registration's validity.

news.title: Built years ago, Noida sector 105 homes now face lakhs in labour cess dues
news.para: In Noida, residents are alarmed to receive labour cess notices for properties constructed many years ago. These notices are issued without any physical inspections or verification, causing confusion since many had already cleared their dues during lease agreements. The sector RWA has formally raised concerns with the Noida DM, while the labour department claims these demands stem from a 2017-18 survey along with current rates.

news.title: Bhubaneswar development body opens Ekamra Residency flat applications, prices disappoint middle class
news.para: The Ekamra Residency housing project by the Bhubaneswar Development Authority is now accepting applications until October 31st. The offering includes 496 apartments, priced from 78 lakh to 96 lakh rupees, which may be challenging for many middle-class families. BDA representatives stress the modern facilities and prime location of the project, highlighting its appeal to prospective buyers despite the high costs.

news.title: Telangana government sets up panel, 30-day deadline to clear 22A property cases
news.para: A new high-level committee has been established to tackle ongoing property disputes. This dedicated team will review cases and provide resolutions within a thirty-day timeframe. Furthermore, a special government order will be issued to address properties that have received prior approvals. Many property owners have encountered issues with registration and transactions, and this initiative seeks to offer much-needed clarity and closure for numerous unresolved matters.

news.title: Mumbai: Decks cleared, Kamathipura redevelopment work set to begin this Diwali
news.para: Mhada has officially signed the construction agreement for the Kamathipura redevelopment project, setting the stage for construction to kick off this Diwali. The initiative aims to provide new homes for over 8,000 residents and businesses while featuring widened roads to enhance transportation and emergency access. Furthermore, the master plan encompasses sustainable utility systems and state-of-the-art amenities to meet modern needs.

news.title: Veegaland Developers shares end 4.5% higher in market debut trade
news.para: Veegaland Developers Ltd shares debuted on Friday with a significant premium. The stock opened higher on both the BSE and NSE exchanges. It concluded the trading day with a notable increase from its issue price. The company's market valuation reached Rs 706.63 crore after the listing. Veegaland Developers Ltd had previously raised funds from anchor investors.

news.title: Walgreens to set up GCC in DLF Downtown Taramani in Chennai
news.para: Walgreens, the renowned American pharmacy chain, has launched its inaugural Global Capability Centre in Chennai, projecting the creation of over 250 technology and operational jobs in its first year. Situated in the DLF Downtown Taramani complex along the OMR GCC corridor, this facility has garnered enthusiastic support from State Industries Minister S Keerthana, who expressed faith in the extensive skill set available in Tamil Nadu.

news.title: BPTP targets ₹3,000-5,000 crore annual sales, ₹1,000 crore rental income in 5-7 years
news.para: BPTP is targeting annual sales of about ₹3,000-5,000 crore while building a larger rental-yielding portfolio, Manik Malik, president and CEO, BPTP, told ETRealty. The company aims to increase annual rental income from around ₹100 crore currently to about ₹1,000 crore over the next five to seven years.

news.title: Panchkula civic body launches extensive survey  in 42 villages to identify building violations
news.para: Panchkula municipal corporation has initiated a comprehensive survey across its 42 villages. Specialized teams are identifying structures built without necessary approvals or maps. Non-compliant property owners will receive notices to regularize or remove unauthorized constructions. The civic body aims for planned and systematic development within municipal limits. Enforcement efforts may face local political pressure despite recent sealing drives.

news.title: Double royalty row: Stone quarries, crushers, m-sand units across Karnataka to shut from September 18
news.para: Starting Friday, all stone quarries and crushers in Karnataka will halt operations due to a protest against the government's dual royalty collection method. Operators are calling for an end to this practice, with plans to block mineral resource imports into the state. This statewide shutdown will persist until a formal governmental resolution is obtained.

news.title: Lucknow civic body collects ₹6.50 crore property tax under OTS scheme
news.para: Lucknow Municipal Corporation has collected ₹6.50 crore in property tax under Uttar Pradesh’s one-time settlement scheme, the highest among the state’s 17 municipal corporations. It has received 3,967 applications so far.

news.title: Bihar government announces one-time settlement scheme for brick kiln operators
news.para: The government of Bihar has introduced a settlement scheme for brick kiln operators, waiving an impressive eighty-five crore rupees in interest on their outstanding dues. To benefit from this initiative, operators are required to settle their remaining principal amounts by December 20, 2026. Additionally, amendments to District Mineral Foundation rules have been made to enhance project allocation, thereby fostering transparency and facilitating development in mining-affected areas.

news.title: Supreme court slams builders for anonymous complaints against judges
news.para: The Supreme Court has initiated an investigation into anonymous complaints targeting judges and lawyers. This stems from the court's examination of builders allegedly abusing subvention schemes. The Chief Justice hinted at a potential CBI inquiry into these complaints, which are suspected to be orchestrated by builders and certain counsel as a tactic to obstruct investigations. The court is committed to thoroughly pursuing these issues until they reach a definitive resolution.

news.title: Building approvals should factor drainage, sewage impact of projects: D. Thara, Housing secretary
news.para: D. Thara, secretary-Department of Capital Development, MoHUA, called for project approvals to assess the additional burden developments create on drainage, sewage and civic infrastructure. She also proposed greater coordination between developers and municipal engineers and suggested pilot projects to quantify and mitigate such impacts.
